summaryHeading: Was your ticket written by El Paso Police? Then it is in Municipal Court
summary: El Paso Municipal Court is the City of El Paso's court of record for Class C misdemeanors and civil parking citations issued within the city limits. Its main office is at 810 E. Overland Ave, phone 915-212-0215.
The court's own page addresses drivers who "received a citation from the El Paso Police Department." Sheriff, DPS and constable tickets go to a Justice of the Peace precinct.
The court states that if you have not entered a plea on every charge by the appearance date on the ticket, you may expect an arrest warrant to be issued. Paying the ticket is itself a plea.
Our flat fee in El Paso Municipal Court is $59 per citation. Extra citations from the same stop are discounted add-ons. Hire online in two minutes.

sections.heading: How to Tell Your Ticket Is in El Paso Municipal Court
paragraphs: Look at the agency printed on the citation. If it says El Paso Police Department, the case belongs to El Paso Municipal Court, whether the stop was on I-10, Mesa St, Montana Ave, Loop 375, Zaragoza Rd or a neighborhood street inside the city limits. The city describes the court as "a court of record which handles Class C misdemeanors and civil parking citations issued within the city limits." That covers speeding, red light and stop sign violations, no insurance, expired registration and cell phone tickets.

If the agency is the El Paso County Sheriff's Office, DPS or a county constable, the case is not here. El Paso County's own instruction is that a citation "issued in El Paso County by an agency OTHER THAN the El Paso Police Department" is handled by the Justice of the Peace precinct the officer noted on the ticket. Horizon City, Socorro, San Elizario, Clint and Anthony police file in their own city courts. Hard to read? Our free ticket and warrant lookup will locate it.

sections.heading: Where the Court Is and How to Reach It
paragraphs: The main office is at 810 E. Overland Ave, El Paso, TX 79901, open Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., phone 915-212-0215 (calls accepted 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.). The city also lists satellite windows inside the police regional command centers: Northeast at 9600 Dyer, Pebble Hills at 10780-A Pebble Hills, Mission Valley at 9011 Escobar, Upper East at 14301 Pebble Hills and West Side at 4801 Osborne, each with its own hours. Confirm hours before you go; they change.

The court's online portal lets you look up a citation, a warrant or a docket date; a separate page takes payments. Looking up your case is harmless. Paying it enters a plea and results in a conviction on your driving record.

sections.heading: What the Court Expects by the Date on Your Citation
paragraphs: Your citation carries an appearance date. The court's payment page puts the consequence plainly: "If you have not plead on all charges shown on the ticket by the appearance date, Pre-Warrant hearing, or Pre-Capias hearing, you may expect an arrest warrant to be issued." A warrant fee is added when the warrant is activated, and a warrant not paid within 60 calendar days is referred to the city's collection agency with an added fee.

The same page lists the rights of a person cited by EPPD: a jury trial (which can be waived), representation by an attorney or yourself, the right to remain silent, and the option to discuss the case with a city prosecutor. Clerks cannot give legal advice. Traffic offenses are described as "generally" punishable by a fine of not more than $200 plus court costs; the amount in any case is set by the court.

sections.heading: What the Court Publishes About Driving Safety Course Requests
paragraphs: El Paso Municipal Court posts its own driving safety course rules. A driver may request the course "by right" before the hearing or before the judge on the court date, but at the moment of the request you must plead guilty or no contest and pay court costs and an administrative fee. The court lists who qualifies by right: 17 or older, a valid Texas driver's license (or active military with a valid license), no commercial driver's license, no driving safety course for a traffic offense in the last 12 months, and no course pending for another ticket.

The court also lists offenses not eligible by right, including speeding 25 mph or more over the limit, passing a school bus, a construction-zone violation with workers present, passing an emergency vehicle, reckless driving, fleeing an officer and leaving the scene of an accident. Outside those lines the driver must appear and ask, and the court's words are: "It will be the judge's discretion whether to grant the course." If granted, the court gives 90 days to return a certified driving record, the TDLR court copy of the completion certificate and a copy of your insurance.
Our deferred disposition and defensive driving page explains both options and why asking for them yourself can cost you a dismissal.

sections.heading: What We Do With a Municipal Court Ticket for $59
paragraphs: When you hire us online or call 915-503-1600, we file a notice of appearance and a plea of not guilty, so the appearance date is satisfied and the court's notices come to our office. At the pretrial docket Robert Navar or a member of our staff confers with the city prosecutor. We read the citation for problems first: a statute that does not match the conduct described, a missing speed or location, an officer no longer with the department. Only when a dismissal is not available do we ask for deferred disposition, a course dismissal or a reduced, non-moving charge. Our goal is to pursue the best available outcome based on the citation, driving record, court and circumstances.

The $59 flat fee covers the appearance, the pretrial negotiation and the paperwork to close the case. Each additional citation from the same stop is a discounted $10 to $30 add-on shown at checkout. Court costs and any deferral or course fee are set by the court and paid to the court. The consultation is free, and se habla español.

sections.heading: Old EPPD Tickets, Warrants and OMNI Holds
paragraphs: Missed appearance dates and missed payment deadlines turn into warrants here, and in general an unresolved case can also be reported to the state's Failure to Appear program, which blocks DPS from renewing your driver's license until the court clears the hold. Warrant recall timing depends on the court's docket; many El Paso courts act within days once an attorney files, but timing cannot be promised.

For $35 for the first warrant and $20 for each additional one, we file the appearance, ask the court to recall the warrant and have the ticket reset onto a docket. See traffic warrant recall and OMNI hold removal.

faqs.q: Where is El Paso Municipal Court and what are its hours?
faqs.a: The main office is at 810 E. Overland Ave, El Paso, TX 79901, open Monday through Friday from 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., phone 915-212-0215. Satellite windows are listed at the Northeast, Pebble Hills, Mission Valley, Upper East and West Side police command centers.

faqs.q: How do I know my ticket is in Municipal Court and not a JP court?
faqs.a: The issuing agency decides. EPPD citations are filed at Municipal Court; El Paso County says a citation from any other agency goes to the JP precinct written on the ticket. Our free lookup form can confirm it.

faqs.q: What happens if I do nothing by the appearance date?
faqs.a: The court's own page says that if you have not entered a plea on all charges by the appearance date or a pre-warrant hearing, you may expect an arrest warrant. A separate Violate Promise to Appear charge can follow. Hiring an attorney before the date satisfies the appearance.

faqs.q: Can I just request defensive driving at the clerk's window?
faqs.a: You can, but the court requires a plea of guilty or no contest at the moment you ask, and some drivers and offenses are not eligible by right. We review the citation for a dismissal first, then request a course or deferral only if that is the better result.

faqs.q: Do I have to appear at 810 E. Overland if I hire you?
faqs.a: Generally not. We file the appearance, handle the pretrial docket and negotiate with the city prosecutor. You would appear only if the case were set for trial, which we would discuss with you first.
